newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, further losses seen.

text.p: Slovenian shares extended their losing streak into the ninth consecutive session on Tuesday amid low liquidity.
Traders said small investors were selling shares ahead of summer holiday season while potential buyers were holding off in the expectation of further price falls.
The SBI index fell 8.86 points, or 0.74 percent, to 1,190.30. The blue-chip index has shed 9.75 percent of its value over the last nine trading sessions.
"The index could fall below 1,000 points by the end of the summer," said Karmen Cerar, a trader at brokerage Poteza.
Overall 12 shares fell, six rose and two were flat, while eight were untraded. Turnover fell to 61.4 million tolars from 73.3 million.
Traders saw no improvement in liquidity until the central bank lifts a ban on foreign investment imposed in February.
Drug maker Lek had the highest turnover. Its shares fell 1.59 percent to 21,650 tolars on volume of 782 shares, for total turnover of 16.6 million. Traders said Lek could fall below 20,000 tolars.
Slovenia's only port operator, Luka Koper, was also among the most actively traded shares. It firmed 0.24 percent to 1,675 tolars on volume of 6,015 shares for total turnover of 10.1 million.
Lek's C issue led the day's decliners, tumbling 6.71 percent to 21,000 tolars on volume of only one share.
Shopping centre operator BTC was the top gainer, firming 2.43 percent to 13,480 tolars on volume of 22 shares in what traders said was a technical correction after Monday's six percent fall.
